#SupplyChain #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
A hidden circuit board. Inside three crypto wallets. 🔌

What BleepingComputer and The Hacker News reported (13 Nov):
→ Trezor confirmed three Safe 5 wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained a malicious hardware implant
→ The extra board sits between the main board and the display and captures the recovery words shown on screen
→ It encrypts them and sends them to an attacker server over a mobile network, retrying until it gets through
→ All three were bought between Aug 20 and Sep 23; 48 CryptoBilis customers have contacted Trezor so far
→ Firmware 2.13.1 (11 Nov) stops these implants capturing anything, but can't protect a phrase captured before it

What to do: if you bought from that reseller, move funds to a new wallet with a new recovery phrase and contact Trezor Support. Buy hardware wallets only from the maker or a channel you can verify.

cover.hook: A 22-year-old bug. Code execution on your Postgres server.
cover.sub: PostgreSQL fixed 52 security flaws in one release. No attacks reported yet.

slides.title: What's fixed
slides.body: PostgreSQL's latest updates fix 52 security flaws. Only one needs no login or user action: CVE-2026-116322, which lets an unauthenticated client restart PostgreSQL 18 servers.

slides.title: The 22-year-old bug
slides.body: CVE-2026-6460 (CVSS 8.8), a type confusion flaw, lets a database user who can create objects run code on the server with the rights of the PostgreSQL OS user. Its root traces back to May 2004.

slides.label: flaws rated CVSS 8.8
slides.note: Researcher Mehmet Ince published a writeup this week. The project hasn't reported any attacks.

slides.title: Clients and cloud too
slides.body: A crafted archive can make pg_restore run code as the user running it. Ince shared proofs of concept with managed services (AWS, Azure, AlloyDB, Supabase, Databricks, Ubicloud) in August.

slides.title: Do this week
items: Rebuild C extensions with the server
Update pg_dump and pg_restore on every machine
Plan off PostgreSQL 14: 14.25 is its last release

items.ig_caption:
Up to 5,000 developers. One fake Claude Code extension. 🧑‍💻

What BleepingComputer reported (14 Nov):
→ Cursor confirmed a breach let attackers place malicious copies of Anthropic's Claude Code extension on the cache serving its extension marketplace
→ Cursor says it started with an access key stored at AI vendor Fireworks AI, then credentials found in old AI agent traces
→ Versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 were live for about 11 hours on Oct 29 and tried to install an SSH backdoor
→ Cursor estimates up to 5,000 users may have received the malicious builds
→ Anthropic's real extension and Open VSX were not compromised

What to do: if you installed or updated it in Cursor on Oct 29, follow Cursor's remediation guide and check for unknown SSH keys. Keep secrets out of AI agent logs and prompts.

cover.hook: Calls and texts diverted. 2FA codes intercepted.
cover.sub: Enea says a state-level group it calls SilentAir used hacked gear inside Asian mobile operators, mostly to spy on people in Taiwan.

slides.title: What happened
slides.body: Stockholm-based Enea found SilentAir's attack sources in at least six Asian countries. Using hacked telecom equipment, it told a target's home network it was now serving their phone, so calls and texts were diverted.

slides.title: Why it matters
slides.body: Enea observed 2FA codes being intercepted right after a diversion took effect, which points to attempts to break into other accounts. Targets were mostly in Taiwan, some political and government VIPs.

slides.label: of SilentAir attacks were interception
slides.note: Versus 2.1% for a typical surveillance company in Enea's earlier research.

slides.title: Who's behind it
slides.body: Enea assesses with high confidence SilentAir is a state-level actor, and links it to China only with low confidence. It says the group has been disrupted for now but could return.

slides.title: Do this week
items: Move VIP accounts off SMS 2FA to app or passkeys
Flag logins right after SIM or number changes
Telecoms: treat the whole IPX as untrusted
Telecoms: link GTP firewalls to SS7/Diameter ones

items.question: Which of your critical accounts still fall back to SMS codes?
